question: Who has written the book Sangeet Bal Prakash?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vishnu Digambar Paluskar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vishnu Digambar Paluskar** was a renowned Hindustani classical musician.
 
• He founded the **Gandharva Mahavidyalaya** in 1901, which was one of the first music schools in India.
 
• He is credited with popularizing Hindustani classical music and making it accessible to the common people.
 
• His book **Sangeet Bal Prakash** is an important contribution to the field of Indian classical music education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hindustani Classical Music:**

 
 
• Hindustani classical music is one of the two major traditions of Indian classical music, the other being Carnatic music.
 
• It originated in North India and has a rich history dating back thousands of years.
 
• It is characterized by its extensive use of improvisation and the raga system, which is a framework for composition and performance.
 
• Some of the well-known forms of Hindustani classical music include Dhrupad, Khayal, Thumri, and Tappa.
 
 
 
• **Gandharva Mahavidyalaya:**
 
 
• Founded by Vishnu Digambar Paluskar in 1901 in Lahore.
 
• It was one of the first institutions to offer formal training in Hindustani classical music.
 
• The institution played a pivotal role in popularizing classical music among the masses and providing a structured curriculum.
 
• The Gandharva Mahavidyalaya continues to be a prominent institution for music education in India.
 
 
 
• **Contribution of Vishnu Digambar Paluskar:**
 
 
• He is known for his efforts to revive and popularize Hindustani classical music in the early 20th century.
 
• He introduced the concept of public concerts, which helped in making classical music accessible to a wider audience.
 
• His efforts in music education laid the foundation for many future musicians and music educators in India.
 
• Paluskar's work and legacy continue to influence the field of Indian classical music today.
